motive: Maria was falsifying shipping manifests, forging Kane's signature, to hide smuggled cargo for a rival crew and skim the fees. Kane discovered it and planned to take the proof to the union board on Monday.
opportunity: Maria left the harbor office before midnight, with the lamp still burning, and was in the warehouse with Kane at 12:00.
method: A cargo hook from the warehouse rack.
verdictNarration: It was Maria Costa, the clerk nobody suspected. For a year she had been cooking the manifests, signing Tommy Kane's name to cargo that never officially existed. Kane noticed. He wrote a letter to Father Anselm and planned to go to the union board on Monday. At midnight Maria left her lamp burning in the harbor office, walked through the fog to the warehouse, and took a hook from the rack. The harbormaster rang her office twice and no one answered. She left a hairpin by the body, and Jack Kane, hiding outside to apologize to his father, watched her walk out.

timeline.event: Jack argues with his father on the pier about money; everyone hears.
Haugen meets Kane in the warehouse about his delayed cargo.
Haugen returns aboard the Nordlys; Paulie starts collecting dues on the pier.
Maria leaves the harbor office with the lamp still burning.
Maria kills Kane with a cargo hook; the harbormaster's call to her office goes unanswered.

clues.name: Forged manifest
clues.text: A manifest for the SS Carolina signed "T. Kane." Hold it to the lamp: faint pencil lines under the ink. The signature was traced.

clues.name: Harbormaster's log
clues.text: The harbormaster's telephone log: "Rang Pier 9 office 12:00 midnight. No answer. Rang again 12:05. No answer."

clues.name: Tortoiseshell hairpin
clues.text: A broken tortoiseshell hairpin on the boards, a foot from the body.

clues.name: Missing cargo hook
clues.text: The hook rack by Bay 4 has one empty peg. The hook beside the body matches.

clues.name: Off-book rum
clues.text: Lashed under a tarp by the Nordlys: twenty crates of Jamaican rum. None of them appear on any manifest.

clues.name: Kane's sealed letter
clues.text: Behind the altar, a letter in Kane's hand: "Father, if anything happens to me, check the Carolina manifests against the cargo. Somebody in the office is cooking the books. T.K."

maria.personality: Polite, efficient, and endlessly cooperative; never raises her voice; gently steers suspicion toward others.
maria.deflection: I'm sorry, detective, I really wouldn't know about that. I just keep the paperwork.

facts.text: I've clerked at Pier 9 for four years. Mr. Kane hired me himself.

facts.truth: I left the harbor office before midnight and was in the warehouse with Kane at 12:00.
facts.lie_text: I was in the harbor office all night filing manifests, from eleven until I heard Paulie shouting at half past twelve.
facts.lie_text_v2: I stepped out onto the pier for some air around midnight. Only the pier. I never went near the warehouse.

facts.unlocked_text: Clerks sign for Mr. Kane when he's busy. Everybody knows that. A signature isn't a murder, detective.
That may be mine. I lose them everywhere. I walk through that warehouse ten times a day.

facts.text: Big Paulie has wanted Mr. Kane's chair for a year. Everyone on the pier knows it.
Captain Haugen's ship has been riding low all week. Heavy cargo, light paperwork.

haugen.personality: Gruff and blunt, impatient with landlubbers, honest about everything except his cargo.
haugen.innocentSecretReveal: Captain Haugen was smuggling rum aboard the Nordlys, and Tommy Kane took a cut to look away. He met Kane at half past eleven and was back aboard his ship by a quarter to twelve. Why kill the man you pay?
haugen.deflection: I am a sea captain, not a gossip. Ask your questions to someone else.

facts.text: Kane moved my cargo. I paid his union. Business, nothing more.
I met Kane in the warehouse at half past eleven about my delayed cargo. By a quarter to twelve I was back aboard the Nordlys.

facts.unlocked_text: Ja, rum. A few crates. Kane took his cut and said nothing. Why would I kill the man I paid?

facts.text: When I left the warehouse, a lamp was burning in the harbor office window. I saw no one inside.
The son. He shouted at his father like a dog barking at the tide.

paulie.personality: Loud, intimidating, loyal in his own way, quick to threaten and slow to think.
paulie.innocentSecretReveal: Big Paulie had been meeting with a rival union local to take over Kane's docks. He wanted the chair, but he wanted Kane alive to hand it over. He was on the pier collecting dues at midnight and found the body at half past twelve.
paulie.deflection: You're askin' a lot of questions for a guy with no friends on this pier.

facts.text: Tommy made me foreman. I'd break any man who touched him.
I was out on the pier from a quarter to twelve till half past, collecting dues. Nobody else out there but the gulls.
Fog thick enough to lose your own hand. But I heard the warehouse door slam around midnight.
Maria? Nah. Nice girl. Brings coffee. Look at the Norwegian.

anselm.personality: Gentle and careful, answers with scripture, guards confidences fiercely.
anselm.innocentSecretReveal: Father Anselm knew Tommy Kane's generous donations came from union dues, and he took them anyway for his parish. He also kept Kane's letter warning that someone in the office was cooking the books. He was at prayer in the chapel all night.
anselm.deflection: Some things are between a man and God, my child.

facts.text: Tommy Kane gave generously to this chapel. I baptized his son.
I was in the chapel all night, at prayer.

facts.unlocked_text: Tommy gave me that letter a week ago. He said someone in the harbor office was cooking the books, and he meant to go to the union board on Monday.

facts.text: Jack came to the chapel at a quarter past eleven, angry, and left again before half past.

jack.personality: Bitter and defensive, lashes out, but cracks when shown he isn't the only suspect.
jack.innocentSecretReveal: Jack Kane came back to the warehouse at midnight to apologize to his father, and lost his nerve outside the door. He saw Maria Costa walk out, wiping her hands. He lied about going home because he thought no one would believe him.
jack.deflection: Why don't you go ask someone who cares?

facts.text: He was my father. Mostly he was the union's.

facts.truth: I came back and was outside the warehouse door at midnight.
facts.lie_text: After the fight I went home. I was there by half past eleven. Nowhere near the warehouse.
facts.lie_text_v2: I walked around in the fog for a while, then went home. I didn't see anybody.

facts.unlocked_text: Fine. I came back to apologize. I was outside the warehouse at midnight and I saw Maria Costa come out fast, wiping her hands on her coat. I thought she'd been crying.

facts.text: I fought with him at eleven on the pier, about money. Everybody heard. That's not a crime.
Ask Paulie where he was. He's wanted the old man's job for years.
